reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a front-running bot as an easy-profit opportunity and instructs viewers to paste contract code into Remix, connect MetaMask, send at least 0.25 BNB to a demonstrated address, and start the bot to receive profits. The speaker reports a successful profit outcome, while the records do not independently establish the bot's behavior, recipient ownership, actual viewer returns, or any resulting loss.

citations.quote: BNB Front Run Bot 2022 Update | Easy Profits in Minutes!
Today I will explain how to use the latest version of the Front Bot.
I recommend not to send less than 0.25 BNB because with lower figures it may not work.
Now click on Action to start the Bot and receive the profits.
Sell automatically triggers at profit and return the profits in your wallet.

opening.argument: Judge the actual wording, not just the headline. The speaker says amounts below 0.25 BNB "may not work," expressly allowing for failure rather than promising that every attempt pays off. The description explains a proposed automated trading process, but neither that description nor the speaker's report of profits establishes what another user would earn. This can be read as a demonstration with a stated operating limitation, not a guaranteed-return offer.

citations.quote: I recommend not to send less than 0.25 BNB because with lower figures it may not work.
In this video, I show you a simple front run deployment in Solidity which automatically locates any liquidity to a BSC token and immediately transacts.
Great, The profits of the bot have arrived.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The headline says "Easy Profits in Minutes," but a headline is not proof of a guaranteed payout or a deceptive recipient. The 0.25 BNB recommendation itself includes the qualification that a lower amount may fail. The reference argument acknowledges that the record does not independently establish the contract's behavior, recipient ownership, viewer returns, or loss. Those gaps matter before treating a conditional demonstration as a proven scam.

citations.quote: BNB Front Run Bot 2022 Update | Easy Profits in Minutes!
I recommend not to send less than 0.25 BNB because with lower figures it may not work.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualification concerns only whether a smaller amount works; it does not warn that sending BNB could fail to produce profits or put the funds at risk. The speaker directs viewers to send funds to the copied address, then presents activating the bot as the way to receive profits. A lack of independently established loss does not erase that funded-profit solicitation.

citations.quote: Let's copy this address. Open MetaMask and click on send. And paste the address.
Now click on Action to start the Bot and receive the profits.

opening.argument: The central presentation is a software walkthrough: the speaker creates a file, pastes code into Remix, selects a compiler, deploys a contract, and connects MetaMask. The sampled screens show the Remix editor and deployment interface. Those concrete programming and wallet steps support reading the video as an operational demonstration. The speaker's reported result is part of that demonstration, not independent evidence that viewers are being paid or that the contract diverts their funds.

citations.quote: Let's create a new file. OK, in this file we are going to paste the code that you will find in the link in the description. Copy this code and paste it on Remix.
Select this compiler version. and compile the file Just wait few seconds. The compilation finished successfully.
Great, The profits of the bot have arrived.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening correctly identifies deployment, wallet connection, and funding steps, but those steps also describe how the demonstrated contract is operated. Its quotes establish what the speaker tells viewers to do; they do not establish that the contract is malicious or that the reported result was fabricated. The visible editor and deployment workflow give the instructional reading substantive support.

citations.quote: Now click on Deploy … and confirm. Good, the contract was created successfully.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Showing programming tools does not make the funding request incidental. The walkthrough moves from deploying code supplied through the description to sending BNB to the resulting address, then explicitly links starting the bot to receiving profits. The sampled screens do not verify that the code performs profitable trades or returns funds to viewers.

citations.quote: Copy this code and paste it on Remix.
I recommend not to send less than 0.25 BNB because with lower figures it may not work.
Now click on Action to start the Bot and receive the profits.

opening.argument: The description offers links to MetaMask, Binance Smart Chain setup, Remix, and contract code: recognizable tools and materials for operating a trading bot. The speaker describes sending BNB to an address copied after contract deployment and says the confirmations mean funds were loaded onto the bot contract. The supplied account does not identify that address as a third-party collection wallet, show a request for credentials, or demonstrate that funds cannot be withdrawn. On this record, an ordinary trading-tool demonstration remains a plausible reading, even if its profit claims deserve skepticism.

citations.quote: Get Metamask here : https://metamask.io/download Connect MetaMask to Binance Smart Chain: https://academy.binance.com/en/articles/connecting-metamask-to-binance-smart-chain Remix : https://remix.ethereum.org/ Contract Link : https://snippet.host/dgug/raw
Good, the contract was created successfully. Here you can find the contract. Let's copy this address.
Confirmations arrived, this means that the funds have been loaded on to the Bot Contract.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats the funding instruction and profit language as decisive. But its cited material does not identify who controls the copied address or establish that the contract diverts deposits. The speaker describes the destination as the newly created contract, while the description says profits return to the user's wallet. Neither assertion is independently verified; that uncertainty cuts against treating the recipient and outcome as established facts.

citations.quote: Good, the contract was created successfully. Here you can find the contract. Let's copy this address.
Sell automatically triggers at profit and return the profits in your wallet.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A contract address need not be identified as a third-party wallet for the pitch to be concerning. The video supplies external contract code, recommends sending at least 0.25 BNB after deployment, and tells viewers to activate the bot to receive profits. The claim that profits return to the user's wallet is the video's own promise, not verification of the contract's operation.
